thread:
maria: Quick sanity check — I'm running a KV prefix-cache warmup comparison (replay harness vs synth traffic) and seeing a weird p99 regression when we flip the mini-kernel selection heuristic. Can folks eyeball methodology?

sam: sure — paste the run id and the exact flags you used.

maria: run id: run-2026-03-12-kv-heatmap-7
S3: s3://redwood-perf/dumps/run-2026-03-12-kv-heatmap-7.tar.gz
Flags: --replay --preserve-order --kv-warmup=prefix --kernel-policy=auto:prefer-mini --batch-target=adaptive

charlie: what does the synth traffic look like vs the replay? sequence lengths / user prefixes?

maria: replay = 12k user traces from prod sampled last week (kept original arrival deltas). synth = poisson arrivals, same per-trace token histogram but no KV prefetch ordering.

anya: Important: replay preserves temporal locality (same user hitting prefixes back-to-back), synth doesn't. That changes prefix hit-rate warmup a lot. Did you run with and without prefix prefetch?

maria: yes. prefetch on for both. Observed HitRate(replay, prefetch)=78% after 60s, HitRate(synth, prefetch)=54%. But when kernel-policy flips to prefer-mini, p99 jumps ~40ms on replay only.

devon: hmm — kernel selection might alter batching behavior (smaller kernels => shorter scheduling quanta) which interacts with KV eviction timing. Can you share flamegraph / timeline?

maria: uploaded flame/trace: https://perf.redwood.internal/run-2026-03-12-7/trace.html
Key snippet from timeline (replay, kernel=prefer-mini):
```
[12:00:03.102] request 4321: kb_fetch start
[12:00:03.118] schedule small-kernel -> batch flush at 12:00:03.130
[12:00:03.131] kv-evict worker: evicted prefix 0x7f from shard-3
[12:00:03.133] request 4321: kb_fetch miss -> fetch remote
```

sam: that eviction right between kb_fetch and remote fetch smells like a race where batching delays pushed eviction into the critical window. Does the replay produce tighter bursts?

maria: yes bursts are denser. synth inter-arrival jitter is larger, so eviction windows rarely align.

perf-ci: New comparison complete. Baseline (kernel-policy=stable) vs candidate (prefer-mini):
- replay: p50 +2ms, p95 +8ms, p99 +42ms, throughput -3%
- synth: p50 -1ms, p95 -2ms, p99 +3ms, throughput +1%
Diffs stored: s3://redwood-perf/compare/run-2026-03-12-7/deltas.csv

charlie: So this is an apples-to-apples question only if the arrival process is identical. We should (a) replay with controlled clock (no original wallclock deltas) to test pure ordering, (b) synth with bursty Poisson to replicate replay burstiness, and (c) run a deterministic eviction tracer to annotate evictions with LRU age and reason.

maria: good call. I'll add a clock-normalized replay (option: --ignore-arrival-deltas) and a synth mode (--poisson-burst-rate=high). Also instrument eviction tracer.

devon: also try a single-shard micro-run to rule out cross-shard eviction interactions. Sometimes kernel scheduler changes CPU affinity and that flips eviction timing.

maria: noted. Plan: three axes -> arrival shape (orig/normalized/bursty-synth), kernel-policy (stable/prefer-mini), shard-config (single/multi). Run matrix and upload heatmaps.

deploy-bot: perf-deploy: started job run-2026-03-13-matrix-1 (CI matrix, estimated 6h).

anya: last note — add a small correctness check under concurrency: random split-prefix lookup + concurrent evict to assert no stale kv reads. Quick script:
```bash
for i in $(seq 1 10000); do 
  spawn_lookup worker lookup_prefix $RND; 
  concurrently_evict_some_prefixes; 
  assert(read_consistent); 
done
```

maria: thanks all. I'll paste the matrix results and heatmaps when run completes. If p99 still regresses only on replay, we'll file a kernel scheduler-eviction bug.

sam: thx — if you need infra help ping me, I can run the single-shard runs. :thumbsup:

maria: will do. :white_check_mark:
